noslope.description: Ablation: TcpRttTrend with the slope trigger disabled (queueing-delay threshold only).

monitor.description: Monitor-only: TcpRttTrend detector running but with NO response; trajectory identical to the baseline, used to measure detection lead time.

S01_light.description: Light load: 1 flow, application-limited to 4 Mbit/s (40% of the bottleneck). No congestion should occur; any early-congestion alarm is a false positive.

S02_moderate.description: Moderate load: 2 flows x 4.5 Mbit/s = 9 Mbit/s offered (about 93% of payload capacity).

S03_heavy.description: Heavy load: 4 saturating flows (each wants 50 Mbit/s).

S04_ramp.description: Rapidly increasing load: 6 flows of 3 Mbit/s start 4 s apart, so the offered load rises 3, 6, 9, ... 18 Mbit/s.

S05_reference.description: Reference: 2 saturating flows, 10 Mbit/s bottleneck, 20 ms delay, 100-packet queue. The capacity, buffer and delay scenarios change exactly one of these.

S10_delay5.description: Short path: bottleneck delay 5 ms, propagation RTT 18 ms (reference otherwise).

S11_delay50.description: Long path: bottleneck delay 50 ms, propagation RTT 108 ms (reference otherwise).
